name: Bengal Foundation
known: Founded in 1986 by industrialist Abul Khair Litu, its chairman, to "promote and showcase Bangladeshi art on a larger platform" (Wikipedia).
Litu chairs Bengal Group Ltd., co-founded AB Bank, Bangladesh's first private bank, in 1981, and chairs the Bengal Institute for Architecture, Landscapes and Settlements (Bengal Institute).

name: Britto Arts Trust
known: The founders say the idea goes back to 2000 and that they started officially in 2002 (On Curating interview with Tayeba Begum Lipi and Mahbubur Rahman, in conversation with Anastasia Baka, Leilani Lynch and Anna Wälli).
Space: the founders began in a living room and had around seven spots, all in residential areas, over about seven years, with moves forced by property owners.
A grant around 2004 to 2005 ran for six years, and Triangle Network co-founder Robert Loder "also donated some funds".
The founders say "Bangladesh does not have any local or public funding at all" (On Curating).

name: Dhaka Art Summit
known: Diana Campbell Betancourt has been artistic director or chief curator since 2014.
Rajeeb Samdani is managing director of Golden Harvest Group, a Dhaka conglomerate with agro, food, IT and logistics companies, which sponsors the summit (Wikipedia).

name: Fresh Milk Art Platform
known: Business Barbados names Annalee Davis as founding director.
The directors are Annalee D.
Co-founded the Tilting Axis conference with ARC Magazine and collaborates with the Ateliers '89 Foundation on Caribbean Linked.
Posts a 2024 report with financial statements, names funders and its three directors; the accounts are compiled by an accountant, not audited.

name: KX Space / Kryly Khalopa Theatre (Prastora KX, closed 2021)
known: Led by director Oksana (Aksana) Gaiko, who calls it the first Free Theatre in Belarus (BGmedia, 8 June 2022).
Director Aksana Haiko.

name: Art-Belarus Gallery (Belgazprombank corporate collection)
known: Viktar Babaryka chaired the bank's board from July 2000 until 12 May 2020 and helped return works by Chagall, Soutine and Léon Bakst to Belarus (Wikipedia).

name: Art-Siadziba
known: Radio Svaboda names Pavel Belavus as founder and first director.
Wikipedia lists Stas Babaytsau, Franak Viachorka and Zmicier Afanasenka as founders.
Kalektar names Belavus as founder and Afanasenka and Viachorka as co-founders.

name: Belarusian State Museum of the History of the Great Patriotic War
National Art Museum of the Republic of Belarus
known: Directors: Uladzimir Prakaptsou (1998 to 2023), then Ganna Konanava (2023 to present) (Wikipedia).

name: National Centre for Contemporary Arts
known: The predecessor Creative Workshops were founded by Mikhail Savitsky, who offered three-year residencies to artists.
Directors: Natalya Sharangovich (2015 to 2017) and Sergei Krishtapovich (2018 to 2025) (Russian Wikipedia).

Nasha Niva adds that it supported experimental projects in visual, theatre and music art, worked with young artists and curators and took part in international projects including Belarus's national pavilions at the Venice Biennale.

Director Siarhei Kryshtapovich, in post since 2018, was commissioner of Belarus's last official Venice pavilion, 'Exit' (2019).

name: OK16 cultural hub
known: Viktar Babaryka, then chairman of the bank's management board, "came up with a proposal to create an art-space OK16 organising exhibitions and theatrical performances" (Wikipedia).
Maria Kalesnikava was its art director (Wikipedia, Nasha Niva).
Babaryka chaired the bank's management board from July 2000 until he resigned on 12 May 2020 (Wikipedia).
Art director Maria Kalesnikava.

name: Ў Gallery of Contemporary Art
known: Valentina Kiseleva was director and curator and Aliaksandr Vasilievič the co-owner and creator (Wikipedia).
CIMAM and the MoMA post say it closed in November 2020, and CIMAM says its art directors left Belarus for security reasons.

name: Netwerk Aalst
known: After about a year and a half closed for renovation, it reopened in March 2024 as NW, with artistic director Laura Herman.
